*Comprehensive data revealing why the Model Context Protocol has become a standard for connecting AI assistants to full-stack application development*


The Model Context Protocol has transformed from an experimental integration standard into a widely adopted way to connect AI assistants with external tools since its 2024 introduction. In July 2026, MCP maintainers reported close to[half a billion downloads](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/) a month across Tier 1 SDKs, demonstrating substantial activity across the developer ecosystem.


Through[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , users can create, edit, and publish full-stack apps with supported assistants including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The assistant handles development while Floot provides managed infrastructure; available actions depend on the connected client's permissions.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Expanding MCP ecosystem:** More than[10,000 active public servers](https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-the-model-context-protocol-and-establishing-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation) were reported by December 2025, reflecting the growing availability of connections between AI assistants and external services.
- **Strong developer confidence:**[72% of surveyed professionals](https://zuplo.com/blog/mcp-survey) expected increased MCP usage, while 54% believed the protocol would persist or become an industry standard.
- **Measurable productivity benefits:** Employees at Block reported[50–75% time savings](https://goose-docs.ai/blog/2025/04/21/mcp-in-enterprise/) on common tasks using MCP-powered tooling, demonstrating potential efficiency gains in AI-assisted workflows.
- **Practical full-stack app development:** Platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) connect compatible AI assistants to managed infrastructure, enabling users to build and publish applications with databases, authentication, storage, and hosting.
- **Rapid MCP adoption:** MCP maintainers reported[nearly half a billion](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/) monthly Tier 1 SDK downloads in July 2026, highlighting the protocol's expanding developer ecosystem.


## **Understanding the Model Context Protocol in App Development**


The Model Context Protocol functions as a standardized connector between AI assistants and development infrastructure. Rather than requiring developers to build custom integrations for each AI model, MCP provides a way for compatible assistants to interact with databases, file systems, authentication services, and deployment tools when those capabilities are exposed by a connected server.


### **What MCP Enables for Conversational Development**


When connected through MCP, an AI assistant can, subject to the available tools and client permissions:


- Read and modify project files in real time
- Provision and query managed databases
- Execute backend functions and API calls
- Deploy changes to live preview environments
- Manage authentication and user systems


This capability changes the development experience. Users can describe an application in natural language while their AI assistant creates project files, writes code, and requests a working preview. Platforms built on[MCP integration](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) handle infrastructure complexity while the assistant handles implementation logic.


## **MCP Ecosystem Growth and Adoption**


MCP adoption statistics reveal how the protocol's ecosystem has expanded across servers, clients, and developer tools. These figures highlight growing integration activity while distinguishing actual MCP usage from broader AI development trends.


### **1. More than 10,000 active public MCP servers by December 2025**


Anthropic reported[more than 10,000](https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-the-model-context-protocol-and-establishing-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation) active public MCP servers in December 2025. This figure documents the expansion of publicly available MCP integrations, demonstrating the protocol's growing infrastructure ecosystem across diverse services and data sources that developers can leverage for their applications.


### **2. Nearly half a billion monthly Tier 1 SDK downloads by July 2026**


In July 2026, MCP maintainers reported close to[half a billion downloads](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/) a month across Tier 1 SDKs. This demonstrates substantial SDK distribution, although downloads are not a count of unique developers, production applications, or companies using MCP.


### **3. Around 14K MCP servers and 300 MCP clients cataloged in June 2025**


A June 2025 research study identified[around 14K MCP servers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23474) and 300 clients in its MCPCorpus dataset. This catalog illustrates the diversity of discoverable MCP integrations, from databases and file systems to specialized APIs and enterprise tools, but is not a live count of every active deployment.


### **4. 1.13 million public repositories importing LLM SDKs in 2025**


The GitHub Octoverse Report documented[1.13M+ public repositories](https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-a-new-developer-joins-github-every-second-as-ai-leads-typescript-to-1/) importing LLM SDKs; new projects using these SDKs increased 178% year over year. This figure measures broader AI development activity rather than MCP adoption specifically, though it indicates the expanding ecosystem in which MCP operates and growing developer interest in AI integration.


## **Enterprise Adoption and Production Deployment Statistics**


Enterprise adoption statistics show how organizations are incorporating MCP into production environments and AI-powered workflows. Survey findings highlight deployment trends, industry differences, and expectations for wider adoption.


### **5. More than 80% of Fortune 500 companies use active AI agents**


Microsoft reports that[more than 80%](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/02/10/80-of-fortune-500-use-active-ai-agents-observability-governance-and-security-shape-the-new-frontier/) of Fortune 500 companies use active AI agents built with low-code/no-code tools. This figure reflects broader AI-agent adoption and does not measure MCP deployment specifically, though it demonstrates the enterprise context in which standardized protocols like MCP operate.


### **6. 72% of surveyed professionals expected increased MCP usage**


The Zuplo MCP Report found that[72% of respondents](https://zuplo.com/blog/mcp-survey) expected their MCP usage to increase over the 12 months following its November to December 2025 survey. This forward-looking confidence suggested continued market interest as technical teams expanded their use of MCP to connect tools, services, and data sources with AI assistants.


### **7. 54% of respondents expected MCP to persist or become an industry standard**


The same survey found that[54% of respondents](https://zuplo.com/blog/mcp-survey) were confident MCP would persist or become an industry standard. This reported confidence helps explain investment in MCP-compatible tools and platforms, though survey opinions are expectations rather than proof of future adoption.


### **8. 41% of surveyed organizations reported MCP production usage**


A Stacklok survey found that[41% of surveyed organizations](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/mcp-adoption-statistics-2026-model-context-protocol) across software, financial services, and retail reported limited or broad MCP production usage. This reflects the surveyed organizations rather than an economy-wide adoption rate, offering insight into early production deployment patterns across multiple industries.


### **9. 45% of surveyed software companies reported MCP production usage**


Stacklok's software-industry cohort showed[45% in production](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/mcp-adoption-statistics-2026-model-context-protocol) , combining limited and broad MCP deployments. This demonstrates production usage among surveyed software companies, but does not establish that every deployment was mission-critical or representative of businesses outside the sample.


## **Developer Community and Ecosystem Growth**


Developer community statistics highlight the growing participation of organizations and individual contributors in the MCP ecosystem. These figures illustrate how open-source collaboration, governance, and community involvement support the protocol's development.


### **10. 305 member organizations of the Agentic AI Foundation in October 2026**


The Agentic AI Foundation reported[305 member organizations](https://aaif.io/news/agentic-ai-foundation-surpasses-300-members) on October 22, 2026. The foundation supports open governance and standardization for agentic AI projects, including MCP, bringing together technology vendors, enterprise users, and open-source contributors to shape protocol evolution and interoperability.


### **11. 2,900+ contributors in the MCP community on Discord**


The official MCP project reported[2,900+ contributors](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/blog/content/posts/2025-11-25-first-mcp-anniversary.md) in its Discord contributor community in November 2025. This community supports discussion, problem-solving, and development of MCP servers, clients, and related tools, while sharing implementation practices across an expanding open-source ecosystem.


### **12. 100+ new contributors joined the MCP community weekly in November 2025**


In November 2025, the MCP project reported[100+ new contributors](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/blog/content/posts/2025-11-25-first-mcp-anniversary.md) joining the community every week. This historical growth demonstrated interest in the protocol as developers discovered its capabilities and organizations invested in compatible tools, though the rate should not be presented as a current 2027 figure.


## **Performance and ROI Metrics from MCP Implementation**


MCP performance statistics examine reported improvements in productivity, task completion, and operational efficiency. Case studies and developer surveys provide insights into potential time savings, resource optimization, and the business value of MCP integrations.


### **13. 50–75% time savings on common tasks at Block**


Block reported[50–75% time savings](https://goose-docs.ai/blog/2025/04/21/mcp-in-enterprise/) on common tasks among many employees using its MCP-powered Goose assistant. This is a company-specific, self-reported result rather than a general MCP performance benchmark, demonstrating the potential productivity impact when tooling is implemented with clear use cases and organizational support.


### **14. Block operated more than 60 internal MCP servers**


Block has reported operating[more than 60 servers](https://nevermined.ai/blog/model-context-protocol-adoption-statistics) , demonstrating how a large organization can use MCP to connect internal tools with AI-assisted workflows. This deployment scale illustrates enterprise MCP architecture patterns, with dedicated servers for services, databases, and internal APIs that support broad AI assistant integration.


### **15. Up to 98.7% token reduction via MCP code-execution patterns**


Anthropic demonstrated[a 98.7% token reduction](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp) in an illustrative scenario by reducing tool-loading overhead from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens. Actual token savings and AI usage costs depend on the implementation and workload, though this example shows how selective tool loading can improve context efficiency.


### **16. 49% measure ROI through developer productivity and time savings**


In the surveyed MCP community,[49% of respondents](https://nevermined.ai/blog/model-context-protocol-adoption-statistics) identified developer productivity and time savings as ROI measures. Reduced context-switching can be valuable when developers use conversational interfaces to work with connected systems, though the result represents survey responses rather than measured productivity gains across all organizations.


### **17. 42% cite enabling new capabilities as a key ROI measure**


Beyond productivity,[42% of respondents](https://nevermined.ai/blog/model-context-protocol-adoption-statistics) cited new capabilities as an MCP ROI measure, such as integrating additional tools and data into AI workflows. These capabilities can help organizations introduce AI-assisted features or enable internal teams to carry out tasks through familiar natural-language interfaces.


## **Technical Implementation and Transport Statistics**


Technical implementation statistics reveal how developers build, connect, and deploy MCP servers across different environments. These findings cover transport protocols, development frameworks, and remote deployment patterns shaping MCP infrastructure.


### **18. 59% of surveyed implementations used Streamable HTTP transport**


The cited survey summary reported[59% using Streamable HTTP](https://nevermined.ai/blog/model-context-protocol-adoption-statistics) transport. This standardized transport supports remote MCP communication between compatible clients and servers, enabling web-based AI assistants to connect to cloud-hosted development infrastructure. The percentage describes surveyed implementations, not a complete census of deployed servers.


### **19. 42% of surveyed MCP builders used FastMCP**


[42% used FastMCP](https://nevermined.ai/blog/model-context-protocol-adoption-statistics) , according to the cited survey summary of MCP builders. This framework simplifies server creation by providing abstractions for protocol handling, allowing developers to focus on implementing the functionality their MCP servers expose to AI assistants.


### **20. 80% of 20 highly searched MCP servers offered remote deployment**


An analysis found[80% of 20 highly searched](https://mcpmanager.ai/blog/mcp-adoption-statistics/) MCP servers. Remote architecture can reduce local installation requirements and support managed services, but this limited sample does not establish that all MCP servers or organizations prefer cloud deployment.


### **21. 180,000+ monthly searches for 20 MCP servers in October 2025**


Search data collected in October 2025 showed[180,000+ monthly searches](https://mcpmanager.ai/blog/mcp-adoption-statistics/) for 20 highly searched MCP servers. This search volume indicates interest from people researching integration options and server implementations, rather than measuring actual installations, usage, or production adoption.


## **Security Considerations in MCP Adoption**


MCP security statistics highlight the challenges organizations face when connecting AI assistants to external systems and sensitive data. Research findings examine authentication gaps, implementation vulnerabilities, and access control concerns affecting secure deployment.


### **22. 50% cited security and access control as a top builder challenge**


A survey of MCP builders found that[50% of respondents](https://zuplo.com/blog/mcp-survey) identified security and access control as a major challenge when developing MCP integrations. This finding highlights the importance of secure authentication, credential management, and permission controls. Developers must carefully evaluate access restrictions and data protection measures before deploying MCP servers in production environments.


### **23. 64% cited security concerns as obstacles in the software industry**


The Stacklok survey found[64% of software respondents](https://stacklok.com/resources/state-of-mcp-in-software-2026/) viewed security concerns and requirements as obstacles to MCP adoption. This concern supports investment in authorization, monitoring, and governance controls that help organizations deploy MCP servers while meeting internal security policies.


### **24. 24% of respondents reported MCP servers without authentication**


The Zuplo report found that[24% of respondents](https://zuplo.com/blog/mcp-survey) were running servers without authentication. This survey finding underscores the importance of access controls, particularly for production deployments where unauthenticated access could expose sensitive data or enable unauthorized modifications to critical systems.


### **25. 43% of tested MCP implementations contained command injection flaws**


Elastic Security Labs cited research finding[43% of tested implementations](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/mcp-tools-attack-defense-recommendations) contained command injection flaws in March 2025. This highlights the importance of implementation reviews, input validation, and appropriate access controls when building or deploying MCP servers, especially those executing system commands or accessing sensitive infrastructure.


## **MCP Security Market Forecasts**


MCP security market statistics examine projected spending, growth rates, and adoption trends across industries and regions. These forecasts highlight anticipated demand for security solutions that protect AI integrations, manage permissions, and support enterprise compliance.


### **26. MCP security market valued at $134.24 million in 2025**


Mordor Intelligence valued the MCP security market at[$134.24 million](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) in 2025. This specialized segment addresses enterprise compliance and risk management needs, providing solutions for authentication, authorization, audit logging, threat detection, and policy enforcement as organizations connect AI assistants to critical systems.


### **27. MCP security market projected to reach $624.46 million by 2031**


The same market is projected to reach[$624.46 million](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) by 2031. This forecast reflects anticipated demand for secure AI integration as MCP deployments expand across industries with strict security and compliance requirements. It is a market estimate, not a guaranteed outcome.


### **28. MCP security market forecast at 29.76% CAGR during 2026–2031**


Analysts project a[29.76% CAGR](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) for the MCP security market from 2026 through 2031. This forecast indicates substantial estimated growth in specialized MCP security products, driven by expected enterprise adoption and the need for controls as AI assistants gain access to sensitive data and systems.


### **29. MCP gateway and runtime policy enforcement held 24.63% share in 2025**


Mordor Intelligence reports that[24.63% of spending](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) in the MCP security market went to gateway and runtime policy enforcement in 2025. This segment focuses on controlling interactions between AI agents and tools through centralized policies, credential management, and request filtering.


### **30. Hybrid MCP security deployments forecast at 31.57% CAGR through 2031**


Mordor Intelligence projects[31.57% CAGR](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) for hybrid MCP security deployments through 2031. This forecast reflects demand for security solutions spanning cloud and on-premises environments, as enterprises use hybrid architectures to balance cloud scalability with local control over sensitive workloads.


### **31. Asia-Pacific MCP security market forecast at 36.53% CAGR through 2031**


The Asia-Pacific market is projected to grow at[36.53% CAGR](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) through 2031. The forecast points to potential growth in regional demand for MCP security controls as organizations adopt AI-enabled workflows and invest in systems that govern access to business data and tools.


### **32. IT and telecommunications MCP security market forecast at 37.62% CAGR**


The IT and telecommunications industry is projected to grow at[37.62% CAGR](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) through 2031, making it the fastest-growing end-user segment in this MCP security market forecast. This reflects projected spending on protection for AI-assisted workflows and connected infrastructure, not overall adoption of MCP in the sector.


### **33. Banking and financial services held 23.71% of MCP security spending**


Banking, financial services, and insurance held[23.71% market share](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) in the MCP security market in 2025. Regulatory and operational requirements help explain demand for secure and auditable connections supporting AI-assisted customer service, fraud detection, and internal workflows.


### **34. Large enterprises held 61.73% of MCP security spending in 2025**


Large enterprises accounted for[61.73% of spending](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/model-context-protocol-security-market) in 2025. In contrast, small and medium-sized enterprises are projected to grow at a 33.29% CAGR through 2031 as organizations seek security solutions that fit smaller technical teams and managed deployment models.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and how does it work with AI assistants?**


MCP is an open standard that enables connections between AI assistants and external tools, databases, and services. With[Floot's MCP integration](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , a supported assistant can read project files, work with databases, execute exposed functions, and request deployment when its tools and permissions allow. This turns natural-language instructions into development actions rather than requiring manual code editing for every change.


### **How does building through an MCP connector differ in billing from other AI app builders?**


Building through Floot's MCP connector uses your existing Claude, ChatGPT, or other compatible AI subscription for model work. Floot separately meters build actions, with Free offering 100 per day, Pro offering 1,000 per day at $25/month, and Power offering 5,000 per day at $100/month. ### **What kind of applications can be built using an MCP-enabled platform?**


MCP-enabled platforms such as Floot can support full-stack web and mobile applications with managed Postgres databases, user authentication, file storage, payments, and deployment. Common use cases include startup MVPs, internal business tools, customer portals, e-commerce apps, and content management systems.[Floot's platform guide](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) explains how the AI assistant handles TypeScript and React implementation while Floot runs the infrastructure.


### **Are there any limitations to using MCP for app development?**


Build actions are limited by plan, complex applications may require multiple iterations, and client permissions can restrict editing or publishing. Custom domains and scheduled jobs require eligible paid plans. Floot's[mobile app guidance](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) describes build allowances and browser setup steps; separate Apple or Google developer accounts are required for store publishing, and store approval is not guaranteed.


### **What are the benefits of using an MCP-integrated code editor with a managed platform?**


Developers using editors such as Cursor can connect to Floot through its[MCP client setup](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/other-mcp-clients) . The editor provides familiar development tools and AI assistance while Floot manages database provisioning, authentication, backend runtime, and deployment. This combination preserves control over coding workflows while reducing the need to configure infrastructure manually; actual capabilities still depend on the assistant's connector permissions.
